blocks.text: A cement mixer's drive shaft carries a heavy gear overhanging its bearing: the gear's tooth force bends the shaft while the motor torque twists it. A point on the shaft surface is pulled by bending and sheared by torsion at the same time, and the shaft will fail where those two combine worst.

blocks.markdown: A circular shaft carrying a bending moment $M$ and a torque $T$ has, on its outer surface, a **normal stress** from bending $\sigma=My/I=32M/(\pi d^3)$ (tension on one side, compression on the opposite, zero at the neutral axis) and a **shear stress** from torsion $\tau=Tr/J=16T/(\pi d^3)$ (the same magnitude all around the surface). At the extreme bending fibre the element is therefore in plane stress with $\sigma_x=\sigma$, $\sigma_y=0$ and $\tau_{xy}=\tau$. Axial force and transverse shear are ignored here; transverse shear is zero at the surface fibre where the bending stress is largest.

blocks.title: Equivalent bending and twisting moments
blocks.text: The principal stresses at the critical surface point depend only on the combination $\sqrt{M^2+T^2}$. Defining the **equivalent bending moment** $M_e=\tfrac12\left(M+\sqrt{M^2+T^2}\right)$ lets the largest principal stress be found as $\sigma_1=32M_e/(\pi d^3)$, as if the shaft carried bending alone. The **equivalent twisting moment** $T_e=\sqrt{M^2+T^2}$ gives the maximum shear stress $\tau_{\max}=16T_e/(\pi d^3)$.

blocks.caption: Solid circular shaft of diameter $d$; $M$ and $T$ in N mm give MPa with $d$ in mm.

blocks.title: Stresses on the surface of a shaft
blocks.prompt: A solid shaft of diameter 50 mm carries a bending moment of 1.2 kN m and a torque of 1.8 kN m at one section. Find the stresses at the surface point where bending tension is greatest, and the principal and maximum shear stresses there.

steps.text: Bending and torsional stresses, with d^3 = 125 000 mm^3.
Radius of the Mohr circle for this element.

blocks.answer: The surface element carries sigma = 97.8 MPa and tau = 73.3 MPa, giving sigma_1 = 137.0 MPa, sigma_2 = -39.3 MPa and tau_max = 88.1 MPa: the combination is much more severe than either action alone.

blocks.markdown: **Where is the critical point?** Because both stresses are proportional to $1/d^3$ and $\sigma$ and $\tau$ are both greatest at the outer surface, the critical point lies on the **surface**, at the section where $\sqrt{M^2+T^2}$ is largest (check the bending moment diagram and where the torque acts), and at the fibre farthest from the neutral axis of bending (top or bottom, where the bending stress is extreme). In a rotating shaft every surface point passes through that fibre once per revolution, so bending stress alternates in sign.

blocks.title: Equivalent moments
blocks.prompt: At the bearing, a shaft of diameter 40 mm carries M = 1.2 kN m and T = 0.9 kN m. Find M_e, T_e, the maximum normal stress and the maximum shear stress.
blocks.answer: M_e = 1.35 kN m and T_e = 1.5 kN m, giving a largest principal stress of 214.9 MPa and a largest shear stress of 119.4 MPa.

blocks.title: Choosing the diameter
blocks.prompt: The loads in the previous example (M = 1.2 kN m, T = 0.9 kN m) act on a shaft whose allowable normal stress is 100 MPa. Find the minimum diameter using the equivalent bending moment, and compare with the diameter from an allowable shear stress of 60 MPa using T_e.

steps.text: From sigma_1 = 32 M_e/(pi d^3) with M_e = 1.35e6 N mm.
From tau_max = 16 T_e/(pi d^3) with T_e = 1.5e6 N mm.

blocks.answer: The normal-stress criterion needs 51.6 mm and the shear-stress criterion 50.3 mm; the larger governs the design for this pair of allowable stresses.

blocks.title: Why combine at all
blocks.text: A shaft under bending alone or torque alone would need a smaller diameter. The equivalent moment M_e is always at least M and at least T/2, and it makes the combined case look like a single-action problem. Which allowable stress governs depends on the material: brittle materials are checked by the largest normal stress, ductile ones usually by the maximum shear stress.

blocks.title: Unit and section checks
blocks.text: Use consistent units (N mm with mm and MPa). Check every section: the largest moment and the largest combined $\sqrt{M^2+T^2}$ may not be at the same place, particularly where the torque is applied by a gear or pulley. Shaft keyways and shoulders raise the local stress and need extra allowance.

points: On a shaft's surface, bending gives sigma = 32M/(pi d^3) and torsion gives tau = 16T/(pi d^3); the two combine on an element at the extreme bending fibre.
The critical point is on the surface at the section where sqrt(M^2 + T^2) is largest, at the extreme fibre of bending.
Equivalent moments simplify design: M_e = (M + sqrt(M^2 + T^2))/2 for the largest normal stress and T_e = sqrt(M^2 + T^2) for the largest shear stress.

questions.stem: For a solid circular shaft of diameter d, which expressions give the surface bending stress and the surface torsional shear stress?

distractorRationale.a: Swaps the factors for bending and torsion.
distractorRationale.b: Correct: S = pi d^3/32 for bending and Z_p = pi d^3/16 for torsion.
distractorRationale.c: Uses the bending factor for torsion; J/c is pi d^3/16.
distractorRationale.d: Uses the torsion factor for bending; I/c is pi d^3/32.

questions.explanation: Bending: sigma = M c/I = M(d/2)/(pi d^4/64) = 32M/(pi d^3). Torsion: tau = T c/J = T(d/2)/(pi d^4/32) = 16T/(pi d^3). The torsional modulus is twice the bending modulus.

questions.stem: Where is the critical point on a shaft carrying a bending moment that varies along its length and a constant torque?

options.text: At the centre of the shaft at the section of maximum moment
On the surface at the free end where M = 0
On the surface, at the section of maximum bending moment, at the fibre farthest from the neutral axis
At the neutral axis of bending

questions.correctOptionText: On the surface, at the section of maximum bending moment, at the fibre farthest from the neutral axis

distractorRationale.a: Both stresses are zero at the centre.
distractorRationale.b: M = 0 there, so only the torsional stress acts, and the combination is smaller.
distractorRationale.c: Correct: bending and torsional stresses are both greatest at the surface, and sigma is largest at the extreme fibre where M is largest.
distractorRationale.d: The bending stress is zero there, so the combination is smaller than at the extreme fibre.

questions.explanation: Torsional shear is maximal at the surface everywhere, so the combination is worst where the bending stress is extreme: at the outermost fibre of the section where the moment is greatest.

questions.stem: A shaft section carries M = 3 kN m and T = 4 kN m. What is the equivalent bending moment M_e = (M + sqrt(M^2 + T^2))/2?

distractorRationale.a: This is sqrt(M^2 + T^2) = T_e, not M_e.
distractorRationale.c: The sum of M and T.
distractorRationale.d: Correct: sqrt(9 + 16) = 5, so M_e = (3 + 5)/2 = 4 kN m.

questions.explanation: The 3-4-5 combination gives sqrt(M^2 + T^2) = 5 kN m. Then M_e = (3 + 5)/2 = 4 kN m, which is the bending moment that would cause the same largest normal stress.

questions.stem: At a surface point of a shaft, bending produces sigma = 80 MPa and torsion produces tau = 30 MPa. What is the maximum in-plane shear stress there?

distractorRationale.a: Adds 40 and 15, which is not how stresses combine.
distractorRationale.c: This is sigma/2 alone, forgetting the shear stress.
distractorRationale.d: This is sigma/2 plus tau, adding magnitudes directly.

questions.explanation: The Mohr circle centre is 40 MPa and the radius is sqrt(40^2 + 30^2) = 50 MPa, which is the maximum in-plane shear stress.

questions.stem: True or false: in a shaft under pure torsion, the maximum shear stress occurs at the outer surface.
questions.explanation: Shear stress is tau = Tr/J, proportional to radius, so it is largest at the surface. This is why the critical point in combined loading is on the surface.

questions.explanation: Because torsional shear acts at the whole surface, the worst point is where bending is also largest. The torque and moment diagrams together locate the governing section.

questions.stem: Derive the equivalent bending moment M_e for a solid circular shaft carrying M and T, starting from the largest principal stress at the surface, and state the circumstances in which it is the appropriate design basis.
markingGuide: States sigma = 32M/(pi d^3) and tau = 16T/(pi d^3) at the extreme fibre
Simplifies to sigma_1 = 16(M + sqrt(M^2 + T^2))/(pi d^3)
Defines M_e = (M + sqrt(M^2 + T^2))/2 so sigma_1 = 32 M_e/(pi d^3)
States it is appropriate for brittle materials governed by maximum normal stress, while T_e is used for ductile materials governed by maximum shear stress
questions.explanation: Substituting the surface stresses into the principal stress expression and factoring out 32/(pi d^3) isolates the moment that would produce sigma_1 in pure bending. The choice between M_e and T_e is a choice of failure criterion.
